question: None shared. P-185 predicts MCI-to-AD conversion within 3 years (pMCI vs sMCI). P-152 reports only cross-sectional diagnostic classification (AD vs HC, MCI vs HC, AD vs MCI) and has no conversion analysis. The channel is shared (MRI: T1 morphometry vs DTI of the superficial white matter both count as MRI), but the task and comparison differ.
metric: Accuracy in both, but on different contrasts: P-185's 69.37% is pMCI vs sMCI; the ledger's 95.8% for P-152 is AD vs healthy controls.

figures.P-185: pMCI vs sMCI accuracy 69.37% (AUC 0.6951), 221 ADNI MCI (126 pMCI, 95 sMCI), 20 x 10-fold CV. Wilson 95% CI with n=221: 0.630-0.751.
figures.P-152: AD vs HC accuracy 95.8% (AUC 0.99) on 48 subjects (24 AD, 24 HC), 5-fold CV; Wilson 95% CI with n=48: 0.860-0.988. MCI vs HC 83.3% (AUC 0.88); AD vs MCI 83.3% (AUC 0.93). No pMCI-vs-sMCI figure exists.

matched_figure_check: Not applicable. P-152 reports no conversion result, so no figure matches P-185's contrast, and P-185 reports no AD-vs-HC diagnostic accuracy.
performance_validity: P-152's cited figure meets the Section 3.5 exclusion: AUC 0.99 (accuracy 95.8%) for AD vs HC on 48 subjects, internal 5-fold CV, no external cohort. P-185's 69.37% passes.
reason: The ledger's claim 'P-152: Acc 95.8 on T2' misreads P-152. The 95.8% separates AD from healthy controls, and the paper contains no MCI-conversion analysis, so there is no shared clinical question to set against P-185's 69.37% pMCI-vs-sMCI accuracy. The cited P-152 figure would also fall under the near-ceiling exclusion (AUC 0.99, n=48, internal CV only). The uncertainty test is not assessed because no shared quantity exists.

quotes.quote: Moreover, the 221 MCI subjects contain 126 pMCI and 95 sMCI subjects.
marker achieved highest accuracy of 69.37% when using SVM classiﬁer with linear kernel.
